title: Quasi-compact opens are closed immersions in quasi-separated schemes with Hausdorff affine charts
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $J$ be a set and $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ an affine open covering of $X$ such that the underlying topological space of each $V_j$ is Hausdorff, meaning that distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods. For every quasi-compact open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], the subset $U$ is closed in $X$ and its original open inclusion $U\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. In particular, the closed subscheme structure is the given open subscheme structure, with its restricted structure sheaf. The empty open and the empty scheme are allowed. The covering need not be finite, and $X$ need not be quasi-compact or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, proof of (1) implies (2): quasi-compact overlaps are closed in Hausdorff affine charts, and an open immersion with closed image is closed. Local closedness generalized to any quasi-compact open, with the finite-neighbourhood argument and local-to-global complement calculation of the returned item, old steps 3 (overlaps), 4 and 5.

proof.text: Fix $j\in J$. The affine scheme $V_j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $X$ is quasi-separated and $U,V_j$ are quasi-compact opens of $X$, [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc] gives that $E_j=U\cap V_j$ is quasi-compact. Its topology as an open subscheme is the subspace topology, whether taken inside $X$ or inside $V_j$.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, proof (1) implies (2), first sentence; replace the first affine open by the given quasi-compact open U.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-compact-subset-hausdorff-closed] in the Hausdorff space $V_j$ to $E_j$. It follows that $U\cap V_j$ is closed in $V_j$ for every $j\in J$.

source.place: Tag 08YB, lemma-quasi-compact-in-Hausdorff (1), used in Tag 0CKV proof (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Each $V_j\setminus U$ is open in $V_j$, hence open in $X$ since $V_j$ is open. As the charts cover $X$, $X\setminus U=\bigcup_{j\in J}(V_j\setminus U)$ is open. Thus $U$ is closed in $X$. This uses an arbitrary union, so the covering need not be finite.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, local closedness argument, expanded by the complement identity.

proof.text: Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the original open inclusion. By [def-weil-open-immersion] its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_X|_U$, and its underlying map is a homeomorphism onto $U$, now closed. For any open $W\subseteq X$ and $s\in\mathcal O_U(W\cap U)$, glue $s$ on $W\cap U$ with the zero section on $W\setminus U$. These two opens cover $W$ and have empty intersection, so the sheaf axiom gives a section of $\mathcal O_X(W)$ restricting to $s$. Consequently $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_U$ is surjective even on sections. The definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] proves that this same $i$ is a closed immersion, with the given open subscheme structure. If $U=\varnothing$, glue only the zero section on $W$; if $X=\varnothing$, the complement calculation is an empty union. No quasi-compactness of $X$ or Noetherian hypothesis was used.
